blockList.listIntroduction: This Ordinance applies to the labelling of the following products as organic products:

item.p: unprocessed agricultural crop and livestock products and production animals;
processed agricultural crop and livestock products intended for human consumption, prepared essentially from ingredients of plant and/or animal origin;

item.num:
c.
Amended by No I of the O of 6 Nov. 2024, in force since 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 687).
item.p:
animal feed materials, compound feedingstuffs and feedingstuffs not covered under letter a and which are used for the feeding of pets and production animals in accordance with Article 3 paragraph 4 letters a and b of the Feedstuffs Ordinance of 26 October 2011.
SR 916.307

content.p:
It also applies to essential oils und to yeasts used for foodstuffs or animal feedingstuffs.
Amended by No I of the O of 2 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 738).

It also applies to unprocessed and processed aquaculture products used for foodstuffs or animal feedingstuffs.
Inserted by No I of the O of 6 Nov. 2024, in force since 1. Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 687).

It does not apply to insects as defined in the foodstuffs legislation and to products from fishing and hunting.
Inserted by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009 (AS 2009 6317). Amended by No I of the O of 6 Nov. 2024, in force since 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 687).

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2000, in force since 1 Jan. 2001 (AS 2000 2491).

content.p: Products under Article 1 may be labelled as organic products if they are produced or imported, prepared and marketed in accordance with this Ordinance.

blockList.listIntroduction: The following indications, their translations in all national languages or usual indications taken from them (such as bio-, eco-) shall be used for the labelling of organic products:

item.p: German: biologisch, ökologisch;
French: biologique;
Italian: biologico;

Romansh: biologic.
Amended by No I of the O of 10 Nov. 2004, in force since 1 Jan. 2005 (AS 2004 4891).

content.p:
The Federal Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research (EAER)

This modification has been made throughout the text. may prescribe a mark which can be used voluntarily for the labelling of products which comply with the provisions of this Ordinance. It may prescribe a special mark for products which are produced in Switzerland.

Labelling, advertising material or commercial documents for products which have not been produced in accordance with this Ordinance may not suggest that such products have been produced organically unless such indications do not relate to the agricultural products in the foodstuffs or feedingstuffs or clearly have no connection with the method of production.
Amended by No I of the O of 26 Nov. 2003, in force since 1 Jan. 2004 (AS 2003 5347).

The labelling may only be used if compliance with the requirements for production, preparation, import, export, storage and marketing of the products has been certified.
Amended by No I of the O of 12 Nov. 2008, in force since 1 Jan. 2009 (AS 2008 5823).

blockList.listIntroduction: The following do not require certification:

item.p: the preparation of products of organic origin at the point of sale, provided that no comparable conventionally-prepared products are prepared in the same production unit and the prepared products are delivered to the consumers solely at the point of sale;
the preparation of foodstuffs and dishes in restaurant and catering facilities;
the storage and marketing of products packaged ready for sale and labelled which are intended solely for Switzerland, provided they do not undergo further preparation before delivery to consumers;
the preparation of certified semi-finished products at the point of sale, provided that no further ingredients are required;

item.num:
e.

item.p: the portioning of openly sold foodstuffs in front of the customer;

item.num:

item.p: the slaughter of animals in slaughterhouses;

item.num:
g.
Inserted by No I of the O of 14 Nov. 2007, in force since 1 Jan. 2008 (AS 2007 6181).
item.p:
internal trade with animals of the bovine species.
Inserted by No I of the O of 10 Nov. 2004, in force since 1 Jan. 2005 (AS 2004 4891).

content.p:
Trade marks with indications in accordance with paragraphs 2 and 4 may only be used if the product was produced in accordance with this Ordinance.
See however Art. 39g below.

article.heading:
Principles
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2000, in force since 1 Jan. 2001 (AS 2000 2491).

blockList.listIntroduction:
The production, preparation and marketing of organic products is governed by the following principles:
Amended by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009, in force since 1 Jan. 2010 (AS 2009 6317).

item.p: Natural cycles and processes are taken into consideration.
The use of synthetic agrochemicals and ingredients is avoided.

item.num:
c.
Amended by Annex No 1 of the O of 27 May 2020, in force since 1 July 2020 (AS 2020 2229).

blockList.listIntroduction: The following may not be used in foodstuffs or feedingstuffs or as foodstuffs, feedingstuffs, processing aids, plant protection products, fertilisers, soil conditioners, plant propagating material, microorganisms or animals:

item.p: genetically modified organisms;
products that have been produced from genetically modified organisms;
products that have been produced by genetically modified organisms.
The products are not treated with ionising radiation and no irradiated products are used.

item.num:

item.p: The number of production animals must be adjusted in accordance with the holding’s own or rented agricultural acreage suitable for the use of farmyard manure.

item.num:
f.

item.p: Throughout their whole life on organic holdings, production animals are kept in accordance with the requirements of this Ordinance and are fed with feedingstuffs which have been produced in accordance with this Ordinance.

item.num:

item.p:
The provisions of the Animal Protection Act of 9 March 1978

blockList.listIntroduction: In this Ordinance, organic holdings are:

item.p: summer pasture holdings as defined in Article 9 AgricTermO, where production is carried out in accordance with the requirements laid down in this Ordinance;

operators that are not holdings as defined in Article 6 AgricTermO and which produce land-dependent products from plant or livestock production, where production is carried out in accordance with the requirements laid down in this Ordinance.

content.p:
Operators that are not holdings as defined in Article 6 AgricTermO and which produce non-land-dependent products or operate aquaculture facilities, provided production in these companies is carried out in accordance with the requirements laid down in this Ordinance, are deemed equivalent to organic holdings.
Amended by No I of the O of 6 Nov. 2024, in force since 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 687).
Organic farming methods must be used throughout the entire organic holding.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 29 Oct. 2014, in force since 1 Jan. 2015 (AS 2014 3969).

article.heading: Exceptions to the principle of total organic production

content.p:
Areas where permanent crops are not grown organically is permitted on an organic holding provided that proof of ecological performance in accordance with Articles 11–25 of the Direct Payments Ordinance of 23 October 2013
SR 910.13 (DPO) is provided for these areas.
Amended by Annex 9 No 14 of the Direct Payments Ordinance of 23 Oct. 2013, in force since 1 Jan. 2014 (AS 2013 4145).

Areas where permanent crops are grown organically is permitted on a non-organic holding provided that proof of ecological performance in accordance with Articles 11–25 of the DPO is provided for the part of the holding which is not farmed organically.
Amended by Annex 9 No 14 of the Direct Payments Ordinance of 23 Oct. 2013, in force since 1 Jan. 2014 (AS 2013 4145).
Areas where permanent crops are grown in accordance with paragraphs 1 and 2 must remain the same for a minimum of five years.

Production of a permanent crop described in letters a–i of Article 22 paragraph 1 of the Agriculture Terminology Ordinance of 7 December 1998
SR 910.91 on a holding must be either totally organic or totally non-organic.

blockList.listIntroduction: The certification body may on application recognise a production facility in a non-organic agricultural holding as an independent organic holding if the production facility:

item.p: is recognisable spatially as a unit of land, buildings and facilities and is separate from other production facilities;
has its own operations centre;
is farmed organically throughout the year and employs one or more persons;
has its own operating income;
has a flow of goods that is independent and separate in space and time from the rest of the holding at all levels of production, preparation, processing, storage and marketing; and

ensures that there is no crossover between the flow of goods from its part of operations and that from the non-organic part.
Amended by No I of the O of 18 Oct. 2017, in force since 1 Jan. 2018 (AS 2017 6083).

content.p:
Before granting recognition, the certification body shall obtain a written opinion on paragraph 5 letters a–d from the canton where the holding is located.
Inserted by No I of the O of 18 Oct. 2017, in force since 1 Jan. 2018 (AS 2017 6083).

Operators under Article 5 paragraph 2 may produce non-organically in parallel to organic production provided the two production areas have a separate flow of goods.
Inserted by No I of the O of 18 Oct. 2017, in force since 1 Jan. 2018 (AS 2017 6083).

The EAER may authorise exceptions to the principle of total organic production in individual cases for research purposes.
Inserted by No I of the O of 18 Oct. 2017, in force since 1 Jan. 2018 (AS 2017 6083).

Holdings which have changed over to organic production are considered to be conversion holdings for two years. A conversion period of two years applies to agricultural acreage, including that which is added to the organic holding. 1 January applies as the conversion date.
Amended by No I of the O of 14 Nov. 2007, in force since 1 Jan. 2008 (AS 2007 6181).

The certification body may authorise a shorter conversion period for mushroom growing and the production of endives and sprouts.
Inserted by No I of the O of 7 Dec. 1998 (AS 1999 399). Amended by No I of the O of 18 Oct. 2017, in force since 1 Jan. 2018 (AS 2017 6083).

The EAER may issue provisions on the requirements for the conversion of algae reproduction and aquaculture facilities.
Inserted by No I of the O of 6 Nov. 2024, in force since 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 687).
The provisions of this Ordinance shall be complied with during conversion.

At the start of conversion, the producer and certification body shall together lay down all the measures which must be taken to ensure that the provisions of this Ordinance can be permanently complied with and verified.

A new conversion in accordance with paragraph 1 is not required if compliance with the provisions of this Ordinance on areas already farmed organically becomes temporarily impossible due to officially imposed measures and the canton waives
Inserted by No I of the O of 6 Nov. 2024, in force since 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 687). reduction or refusal of direct payments due to force majeure in accordance with Article 106 paragraphs 1 and 2 letter f DPO.
SR 910.13

If the integrity of the organic products is jeopardised by officially imposed measures in accordance with paragraph 4, a new conversion period of two years shall apply to the area affected by the measures.
Inserted by No I of the O of 6 Nov. 2024, in force since 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 687).

If immediate total conversion involves unacceptably high risks, an organic holding growing vines, fruit, vegetables or ornamental plants may convert to organic production in stages. The entire holding must be fully converted within five years, with the exception of holdings referred to in Article 7 paragraph 1.

The certification body shall decide whether to authorise conversion in stages.
Amended by No I of the O of 18 Oct. 2017, in force since 1 Jan. 2018 (AS 2017 6083).

blockList.listIntroduction: In particular, the following conditions must be met:

item.p: a binding conversion plan is drawn up with a detailed description of the conversion stages and a timetable;
any contamination of organic parcels with unauthorised agrochemicals is avoided;
areas farmed in different ways are clearly marked out;
products produced under different methods are harvested and stored separately;

item.num:
e.
Amended by Annex 9 No 14 of the Direct Payments Ordinance of 23 Oct. 2013, in force since 1 Jan. 2014 (AS 2013 4145).

item.p: a sample is taken each year for analysis of the residues in organically produced products;

item.num:
g.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2000, in force since 1 Jan. 2001 (AS 2000 2491).
item.p: the requirements laid down in the Annex are met.

content.p:
If immediate total conversion of livestock production is not reasonable, the certification body may allow the holding to convert livestock farming in stages according to animal categories within three years.
Amended by No I of the O of 18 Oct. 2017, in force since 1 Jan. 2018 (AS 2017 6083).

blockList.listIntroduction: Parallel production of the following is not permitted:

item.p: varieties which are not clearly distinguishable;

animals of the same category of production animal.
Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2000, in force since 1 Jan. 2001 (AS 2000 2491).

article.heading: Fertility and biological activity of the soil

blockList.listIntroduction: The fertility and biological activity of the soil shall be maintained and, if possible, increased. To this end, the following measures in particular shall be taken:

item.p: the soil shall be cultivated in such a way that it maintains sustainable productivity due to its physical, chemical and biological properties;
biological diversity shall be encouraged;
in land cultivation, soil cover shall be sufficient to ensure that soil erosion, and losses of nutrients and plant protection products are kept to the minimum;
the intensity of the production of fodder crops shall be varied and adapted to the location.

content.p:
Organic plant production shall be practised in living soil in connection with the subsoil and bedrock.
Inserted by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009 (AS 2009 6317). Amended by No I of the O of 2 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 738).

Cultivation methods in which plants that do not naturally grow in water have their roots in a nutrient solution only or in an inert medium to which a nutrient solution is added (hydroponic production) are prohibited.
Inserted by No I of the O of 2 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 738).

blockList.listIntroduction: By way of derogation from paragraph 2, the following practices shall be allowed:

item.p: growing plants for the production of ornamentals and herbs in pots to be sold together with the pots to consumers;
growing seedlings or saplings in containers for further transplanting;

producing germinated seeds, in particular shoots, sprouts and cress, that rely exclusively on the seed nutrient reserves, by moistening of seeds in clear water, provided that the seeds meet the requirements of this Ordinance;

producing forced chicory, including by dipping in clear water, provided that the plant propagating material and the substrate meet the requirements of this Ordinance.
Inserted by No I of the O of 2 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 738).

blockList.listIntroduction: Pests, diseases and weeds must be controlled by a combination of different measures, in particular the following:

item.p: a choice of appropriate species and varieties;
appropriate crop rotation;

item.num:
c.
Amended by No I of the O of 2 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 738).
item.p: physical cultivation procedures;
thermal procedures where steaming of the soil is restricted to market gardening under cover and production of seedlings;
promotion and protection of natural enemies of pests through provisions favourable to them (e.g. hedges, nesting sites, release of predators).

content.p:
The EAER shall specify authorised plant protection products and instructions for their use. Substances which are not of plant, animal, microbial or mineral origin and are not identical to their natural form shall only be authorised if their conditions of use preclude any contact with the edible parts of the plant. This applies without prejudice to the authorisation procedure laid down in the Plant Protection Products Ordinance of 18 May 2005
[AS 2005 3035, 4097, 5211; 2006 4851; 2007 821 No III, 1469 Annex 4 No 54, 1843 4541, 6291, 2008 2155, 4377 Annex 5 No 11, 5271; 2009 401 Annex No 3 2845; 2010 2101. AS 2010 2331 Art. 84]. See now: the O of 12 May 2010 (SR 916.161). .
Amended by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009, in force since 1 Jan. 2010 (AS 2009 6317).
Plant protection products may only be used in the case of immediate danger threatening the crops.
The use of growth regulators, wilting products and herbicides is not permitted.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 26 Nov. 2003 (AS 2003 5347). Amended by Annex 9 No 14 of the Direct Payments Ordinance of 23 Oct. 2013, in force since 1 Jan. 2014 (AS 2013 4145).

content.p:
The requirements on the spray test and the rinse water tank for power take-off or self-propelled equipment used for plant protection have to be accomplished according to Annex 1 figure 6.1 DPO
SR 910.13 . Demeter holdings which only use their equipment to apply biodynamic preparations are exempt.
Where possible, organic fertilisers such as farmyard manure and compost must come from the holding itself.

The EAER shall specify the fertilisers that are authorised and the instructions for their use. Mineral nitrogen fertilisers may not be used.
Amended by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009, in force since 1 Jan. 2010 (AS 2009 6317).

Fertiliser requirements have to be proved on the basis of a nutrient balance according to Article 13 DPO
SR 910.13 and the requirements according to Annex 1 number 2 DPO.
Amended by Annex 9 No 14 of the Direct Payments Ordinance of 23 Oct. 2013, in force since 1 Jan. 2014 (AS 2013 4145).

The quantity of nutrients applied per hectare (own farmyard manure and manure from other farms, bought fertilisers) may, under the most favourable valley conditions, correspond to no more than 2.5 livestock manure units (LMU). It shall be graded according to soil load capacity, altitude and topographical conditions. If maximum values laid down by the Canton under water pollution control legislation are lower, these apply.
Suitable products based on microorganisms or plants such as biodynamic preparations, and mineral powders may be used to activate compost or soil.

Farmyard manure may only be supplied by and to holdings which provide the ecological services laid down in the DPO.
Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2000 (AS 2000 2491). Amended by Annex 9 No 14 of the Direct Payments Ordinance of 23 Oct. 2013, in force since 1 Jan. 2014 (AS 2013 4145).

article.heading: Seeds, plants and plant propagating material

content.p: Seeds, plants and plant propagating material must come from organic holdings.

In the case of seeds, the mother plants, and in the case of plant propagating material, the parent plants must have been cultivated in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter for at least a generation or for the duration of two plant cycles in the case of perennial crops.

In derogation from paragraph 1, plant material which has been propagated in-vitro and certified in accordance with the Seeds Ordinance of 7 December 1998
SR 916.151 may be used.
Amended by No I of the O of 7 Dec. 1998, in force since 1 Jan. 1999 (AS 1999 399).

…
Inserted by No I of the O of 26 Nov. 2003 (AS 2003 5347). Repealed by No I of the O of 6 Nov. 2024, with effect from 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 687).
This applies without prejudice to the requirements of the Seeds Ordinance.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 26 Nov. 2003 (AS 2003 5347). Amended by No I of the O of 6 Nov. 2024, in force since 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 687).

article.heading: Use of non-organic seeds and non-organic plant propagating material

blockList.listIntroduction: Any person who wishes to use non-organic seeds or non-organic plant propagating material must provide evidence that:

item.p: no suitable organically produced seeds or organic plant propagating material are available; or
no one is able to deliver the seeds or the propagating material before sowing or planting, although they were ordered in good time.

content.p: Valid evidence under paragraph 1 must be provided using the details on availability in the information system described in Article 33a.

If, according to the details in the information system described in Article 33a, the variety users wish to procure is not available as organic seeds or organic plant propagating material, but other varieties of the same species are available, users may use non-organic seeds or non-organic plant propagating material only if they can explain why none of the organic varieties of the same species are suitable in particular for the relevant agronomic and pedoclimatic conditions, and why none of the species has the technological characteristics required for the planned production.

Any person who uses non-organic seeds or plant propagating material must notify the operator of the information system described in Article 33a of the quantity of seed or plant propagating material used and the variety.

On request, the Research Institute of Organic Agriculture (FiBL) may authorise the use of non-organic seeds or non-organic plant propagating material, provided this enables research into variety preservation or product innovation as part of small-scale field trials.

blockList.listIntroduction: Non-organic plant propagation material may be used only if it has not been treated with plant protection products; this does not apply to:

item.p: treatments which are authorised for organic farming; and
treatments which for reasons of plant health are prescribed for all varieties of a particular species in the production area.

article.heading:
Collection of wild plants and wild algae
Amended by No I of the O of 6 Nov. 2024, in force since 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 687).

blockList.listIntroduction: Collection of edible wild plants and plant parts which grow naturally in forests and on agricultural land are deemed to be production within the context of organic farming if:

item.p: this land has not been treated with unauthorised products for three years preceding collection; and
collection does not prejudice the stability of the natural environment and the conservation of species in the collection area.

content.p: The collection area must be geographically defined.
The collection process must be thoroughly documented.
The inspection procedure for organic holdings shall be applied as appropriate.

The EAER may issue further provisions on the requirements for gathering wild algae and the applicable inspection procedure.
Inserted by No I of the O of 6 Nov. 2024, in force since 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 687).

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2000, in force since 1 Jan. 2001 (AS 2000 2491).

content.p:
Bovine species, including bubalus and bison species, equine species, sheep, goats, porcine species and poultry shall be kept in accordance with the provisions on regular outdoor exercise of Article 75 DPO
SR 910.13 and the requirements according to Annex 6 DPO. The provisions on particularly animal friendly housing systems of Article 74 DPO and the requirements of Annex 6 DPO apply to the keeping of rabbits.
Amended by Annex 9 No 14 of the Direct Payments Ordinance of 23 Oct. 2013, in force since 1 Jan. 2014 (AS 2013 4145).

blockList.listIntroduction: The EAER may issue additional regulations for:

item.p: livestock housing;
stock-keeping and breeding;
grazing and outdoor runs.

content.p:
Rules for stockfarming may also be issued for the other categories of livestock.
Amended by No I of the O of 7 Nov. 2001, in force since 1 Jan. 2002 (AS 2001 3542).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2000, in force since 1 Jan. 2001 (AS 2000 2491).

content.p: It is not permitted to keep animals tethered.

blockList.listIntroduction: In agreement with the certification body, however, the following may be kept tethered:

item.p: individual animals for a limited period for reasons of safety or animal welfare;

item.num:
b.
Amended by Annex 9 No 14 of the Direct Payments Ordinance of 23 Oct. 2013, in force since 1 Jan. 2014 (AS 2013 4145).
item.p:
animals of the bovine species, provided the provisions on regular outdoor exercise laid down in Article 75 DPO
SR 910.13 are complied with.

content.p:
...
Repealed by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009, with effect from 1 Jan. 2010 (AS 2009 6317).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 7 Nov. 2001 (AS 2001 3542). Amended by No I of the O of 6 Nov. 2024, in force since 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 687).

content.p:
If animals are put to summer pasture, the requirements of Articles 26–33 DPO
SR 910.13 must be complied with. If possible, the summer pasture must be on organic holdings.

If animals are not put to summer pasture on organic holdings, it must be ensured that the products manufactured in accordance with this Ordinance are labelled as organic only if a guarantee of a separate goods flow can be provided.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2000, in force since 1 Jan. 2001 (AS 2000 2491).

content.p: The fodder must meet the physiological nutritional requirements of the livestock at various stages of their development and must be intended to ensure quality production rather than maximising production.
Force-feeding and keeping of livestock under conditions which could lead to anaemia is not permitted.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2000, in force since 1 Jan. 2001 (AS 2000 2491).

content.p: The EAER shall lay down which feedingstuffs are permitted and how feedingstuffs are used.

It may prohibit the use of certain feed additives and processing aids, and certain processing methods.
Amended by No I of the O of 31 Oct. 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 6353).

blockList.listIntroduction: In derogation from the principle laid down in Article 3 letter c, it may authorise feed additives and processing aids which have been produced using genetically modified organisms if:

item.p: they cannot be replaced by other substances; and

they are not available on the market manufactured in any other way.
Amended by No I of the O of 31 Oct. 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 6353).

content.p:
The purchase of feedingstuffs to supplement the holding’s own feed stocks is permitted. Purchases must be from organically produced crops and if possible from the same region. For the purposes of harmonisation with the relevant EU legislation, the EAER may make provision that a limited percentage of non-organic animal feedingstuffs may be purchased.
Amended by No I of the O of 31 Oct. 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 6353).

The addition of feedingstuffs from conversion holdings is permitted on average up to a maximum of 30 per cent of the ration of individual categories of production animal, as dry matter. If this feedingstuff is from the holding itself, the amount may be 60 per cent, and, where this is a conversion holding, 100 per cent.
Amended by No I of the O of 31 Oct. 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 6353).

In case of proven fodder yield losses, especially due to exceptional weather conditions, the directly affected livestock farmer may use non-organic fodder for a limited period with the prior written agreement of the certification body, provided that the livestock farmer is able to satisfy the certification body that insufficient organic fodder is available. If whole areas are affected by fodder yield losses, the Federal Office for Agriculture (FOAG) may also grant permission for the area.
Amended by No I of the O of 6 Nov. 2024, in force since 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 687).

Fodder ingredients must be left natural and fodder preparation methods used must be as natural and energy-saving as possible. Feedingstuffs may not contain any traces of genetically modified organisms or of secondary products of genetically modified organisms which proportionally are higher than the maximum levels for unavoidable impurities laid down in legislation on feedingstuffs.

Sheep may temporarily graze in nomadic herds on non-organically farmed areas. The amount of fodder consumed, as dry matter, may not exceed 10 per cent of the total annual fodder intake.
Inserted by No I of the O of 14 Nov. 2007 (AS 2007 6181). Amended by No I of the O of 6 Nov. 2024, in force since 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 687).

The proportion of non-organically grown fodder may amount to 10 per cent of the total fodder consumption for retired horses.
Inserted by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009, in force since 1 Jan. 2010 (AS 2009 6317).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2000, in force since 1 Jan. 2001 (AS 2000 2491).

content.p: Ruminants must receive at least 60 per cent of fodder dry matter in the form of roughage, fresh or dried fodder or silage.

The feeding of young mammals must be based on natural milk, preferably maternal milk. All mammals must be fed for a minimum period on natural milk. The minimum period depends on the animal species. It shall be three months for bovines (including bubalus and bison species) and equines, 35 days for sheep and goats and 40 days for pigs.
For poultry, the feed formula used in the fattening stage must consist of 65 percent grain and grain legumes (their products and by-products) as well as oil seeds (their products and by-products).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2000, in force since 1 Jan. 2001 (AS 2000 2491).

content.p: The health and productivity (life output) of livestock and the quality of livestock products must be promoted by the selection of suitable breeds and breeding methods.
Reproduction of livestock must be based on natural methods.

Artificial insemination is permitted. Other forms of artificial or otherwise influenced reproduction (e.g. embryo transfer) are not permitted. They may be used with the prior written agreement of the certification body if this is necessary to preserve endangered genetic resources. Affected animals and their products may not be marketed with any reference to organic farming.
Amended by No I of the O of 10 Nov. 2004, in force since 1 Jan. 2005 (AS 2004 4891).

No livestock produced from embryo transfer shall be brought in, with the exception of animals of the bovine species in a rearing contract with a non-organic holding. In this case, the animals must return to the original holding after a period laid down in the contract. Animals from embryo transfer which were already kept on the holding before conversion of the holding may still be kept until their departure according to the provisions of this Ordinance.
Amended by No I of the O of 7 Nov. 2001, in force since 1 Jan. 2002 (AS 2001 3542).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2000, in force since 1 Jan. 2001 (AS 2000 2491).

blockList.listIntroduction: Disease prevention must be based on the following principles:

item.p: selection of suitable breeds or strains;
application of animal husbandry practices appropriate to the requirements of each species, encouraging strong resistance to disease and the prevention of infections;
the use of high-quality feed, together with regular exercise (pasture, outdoor run, outdoor climate area) to encourage the natural immunological defence of livestock;
ensuring an appropriate density of livestock, thus avoiding overstocking and any resulting animal health problems.

content.p: If an animal becomes sick or injured, it must be treated immediately, if necessary in isolation, and in suitable housing.

blockList.listIntroduction: The use of veterinary medicinal products in organic stockfarming shall comply with the following principles:

item.p: Phytotherapeutic products (e.g. plant extracts, excluding antibiotics, or plant essences), homeopathic products (e.g. plant, animal and mineral substances) and trace elements and products laid down by the EAER for this purpose shall be used in preference to chemically-synthesised allopathic veterinary medicinal products or antibiotics, provided that their therapeutic effect is shown to be effective for the species of animal and the condition for which the treatment is intended.

If the use of the products listed in letter a should not prove to be effective in combating illness or injury, but treatment is essential to prevent suffering or distress to the animal, chemically-synthesised allopathic veterinary medicinal products or antibiotics may be used under the responsibility of a veterinarian.

item.num:
c.
Amended by No I of the O of 29 Oct. 2014, in force since 1 Jan. 2015 (AS 2014 3969).
item.p: The use of coccidiostatics and the use of hormones or similar substances to control reproduction (e.g. induction or synchronisation of oestrus), or for other purposes, is not permitted. Nevertheless, hormones may be administered to an individual animal as a form of therapeutic veterinary treatment.
The use of chemically-synthesised allopathic veterinary medicinal products or antibiotics for preventive treatments is not permitted.

content.p: The type of product (including an indication of the active pharmacological substances involved) together with details of the diagnosis, the method of administration, the duration of the treatment and the prescribed withdrawal period must be recorded clearly and indelibly in writing in the treatment book.
Livestock treated must be clearly identified as such at all times – individually in the case of large animals, individually or as a group, in the case of poultry or small animals.
Vaccination and worming is permitted where there is an existing animal health risk.

...
Repealed by No I of the O of 26 Oct. 2011, with effect from 1 Jan. 2012 (AS 2011 5309).

The withdrawal period between the last administration of a chemically-synthesised allopathic veterinary medicinal product under normal conditions of use, and the production of organically produced foodstuffs from such animals must be twice the legal withdrawal period. This does not apply to the use of products to dry up cows with udder problems.

With the exception of vaccinations, treatments for parasites, anaesthetic agents, pain relief treatments and treatments as part of state livestock epidemic programmes, where an animal or group of animals receives more than three courses of treatments with chemically-synthesised allopathic veterinary medicinal products or antibiotics within one year (or more than one course of treatment if their production lifecycle is less than one year), the livestock concerned, or produce derived from them, shall not be sold as being produced in accordance with this Ordinance, and the livestock must undergo the conversion periods laid down in Article 16f paragraph 2.
Amended by No I of the O of 12 Nov. 2008, in force since 1 Jan. 2009 (AS 2008 5823).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2000, in force since 1 Jan. 2001 (AS 2000 2491).

content.p: Zootechnical procedures shall be kept to the minimum. They must be carried out by qualified personnel at the age most appropriate for the animal.

Procedures such as docking tails, clipping teeth and, in the case of poultry, beaks, toes and wings, castration, the dehorning of adult animals and the use of nose rings and the fitting of clips and wires in the nose ring for pigs is not permitted.
Amended by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009, in force since 1 Jan. 2010 (AS 2009 6317).

In justified cases, the dehorning of adult animals for safety reasons is permitted, provided that it is conducted properly under anaesthetic by a veterinary surgeon and not during the months of May, June, July and August.
Inserted by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009, in force since 1 Jan. 2010 (AS 2009 6317).

blockList.listIntroduction: The following procedures may be carried out on individual animals:

item.p: attaching elastic bands to the tails of sheep, if this is necessary to improve the health, welfare or hygiene of the livestock;

item.num:
b.
Amended by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009, in force since 1 Jan. 2010 (AS 2009 6317).
item.p: dehorning of young animals, except for yaks, water buffalo and bison, under anaesthetic, if this is necessary for reasons of safety;

item.num:
c.
Amended by No I of the O of 27 Oct. 2010, in force since 1 Jan. 2011 (AS 2010 5859).
item.p: castration in order to maintain the quality of products.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009, in force since 1 Jan. 2010 (AS 2009 6317).

article.heading: Practical trials relating to vaccination against sexual odour

content.p: For the period up to 31 December 2012, FOAG may authorise limited practical trials on organic holdings for vaccination against sexual odour, particularly for the purpose of researching questions relating to ethology, efficiency, profitability and product quality.

Applications for trials may be made by an independent scientific institution which has responsibility for the trial. The application shall set out the aims of the trial and the test methods together with the organic holdings and number of animals taking part.
The marketing history of the vaccinated animals must be fully documented through to the final vendor. The products concerned shall not be exported.
FOAG may lay down further requirements and conditions for the practical trials.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2000, in force since 1 Jan. 2001 (AS 2000 2491).

content.p:
Only production animals which come from organic holdings may be kept. This does not apply to horses for riding and draught horses, hobby animals, and animals of the bovine species in rearing contract with a non-organic holding. In this case, the animals must return to the original holding after a period laid down in the contract.
Amended by No I of the O of 7 Nov. 2001, in force since 1 Jan. 2002 (AS 2001 3542).

blockList.listIntroduction: Production animals which do not come from organic holdings, and which are brought in after conversion has begun, must be reared for the following periods in accordance with the rules of this Ordinance:

item.p: equine and bovine species (including bubalus and bison species) for meat production for 12 months and at least three quarters of their lives;
small ruminants and pigs for at least 6 months;
milk-producing animals for at least 6 months;
poultry for meat production, brought in when less than three days old, for at least 56 days;
poultry for egg production for at least 6 weeks.

content.p:
...
Repealed by No I of the O of 10 Nov. 2004, with effect from 1 Jan. 2005 (AS 2004 4891).

When insufficient numbers of organically reared animals are available for supplementing natural growth or for the renewal of the herd or flock, in agreement with the certification body, female nulliparous young animals from non-organic-production stockfarms may be brought in throughout the year subject to a maximum of 10 per cent of the adult equine or bovine livestock, including bubalus and bison species, or 20 per cent of the adult porcine, ovine or caprine livestock. For organic holdings with fewer than 10 bovine or equine animals or with fewer than five porcine, ovine or caprine animals, renewal shall be limited to one animal per year.

blockList.listIntroduction: With the prior written agreement of the certification body, a holding may house animals from non-organic holdings up to a maximum of 40 per cent of the total number when animals from organic holdings are not available in the following cases:

item.p: major expansion of stock keeping;
change of breed;
development of a new branch of animal production;
necessity of a substitute calf for a mother or fester cow;

danger that a particular breed will be lost to agriculture.
Amended by No I of the O of 10 Nov. 2004, in force since 1 Jan. 2005 (AS 2004 4891).

content.p:
In the case of a high mortality rate caused by an epidemic or catastrophic circumstances, with the prior written agreement of the certification body, livestock numbers may be renewed or reconstituted with animals from non-organic holdings, when animals from organic holdings are not available.
Amended by No I of the O of 10 Nov. 2004, in force since 1 Jan. 2005 (AS 2004 4891).
Males for breeding may be bought in from non-organic-production holdings at any time.

If insufficient numbers of birds from organic holdings are available, poultry from non-organic holdings may be purchased in order to reconstitute livestock numbers, provided that the chicks are installed no later than three days after birth.
Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Nov. 2005 (AS 2005 5527). Amended by No I of the O of 14 Nov. 2007, in force since 1 Jan. 2008 (AS 2007 6181).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2000, in force since 1 Jan. 2001 (AS 2000 2491).

article.heading: Minimum age at slaughter for poultry

blockList.listIntroduction: For poultry, the minimum age at slaughter shall be:

item.p: 81 days for broilers;
49 days for Peking ducks;
70 days for female Muscovy ducks;
84 days for male Muscovy ducks;
92 days for mallards;
94 days for guineafowl;
140 days for turkeys and geese.

content.p: Producers who do not apply these minimum slaughter ages must use slow-growing strains.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 7 Nov. 2001, in force since 1 Jan. 2002 (AS 2001 3542).

content.p: The EAER may allow exceptions to the principle of total organic production and total organic conversion for beekeeping.

It may lay down further provisions regarding the feeding of bees, the siting of apiaries, animal health, the origin of the bees, identification and inspection, extraction, processing and storage of beekeeping products.
It may require that products produced in certain areas or regions may not be marketed with the reference to organic farming.

section.num:
Section 5
Inserted by No I of the O of 6 Nov. 2024, in force since 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 687).
section.heading: Aquaculture

blockList.listIntroduction: The EAER may issue provisions on:

item.p: the requirements for the production and reproduction of algae produced in aquaculture;
the requirements for the production, origin, livestock feeding and animal health of aquaculture animals and for animal husbandry practices;
the applicable inspection procedures.

chapter.num:
Chapter 2a
Inserted by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009, in force since 1 Jan. 2010 (AS 2009 6317).
chapter.heading: Requirements for the Processing of Foodstuffs and Animal Feedingstuffs

article.heading: Specific principles for the production of processed organic foodstuffs

blockList.listIntroduction: In addition to the general principles laid down in Article 3, the following principles apply to the production of processed organic foodstuffs:

item.p: Organic foodstuffs must be made from organically produced ingredients, unless an ingredient is not available on the market as an organic product.

The use of foodstuff additives, non-organic ingredients with primarily technical and sensory functions, micronutrients and processing aids must be kept to a minimum and limited to cases where this is a major technological requirement or is for particular nutritional purposes.
Substances and production processes which could be misleading with regard to the actual nature of the product are not permitted.
The foodstuffs must be processed with care, preferably using organic, mechanical and physical methods.

item.num:
e.
Inserted by No I of the O of 2 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 738).
item.p: The use of ingredients or substances that contain or consist of engineered nanomaterials is prohibited.

article.heading: Provisions for the production of processed organic foodstuffs

content.p: The production of processed organic foodstuffs must be carried out separately in time or space from that of non-organic foodstuffs.

blockList.listIntroduction: Processed organic foodstuffs must meet the following requirements:

item.num:
a.
Amended by No I of the O of 2 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 738).
item.p: The product must be made predominantly from ingredients of agricultural origin; added water and sodium chloride are not taken into account when deciding whether a product is made predominantly from ingredients of agricultural origin. Yeast and yeast products as well as flavourings shall be included as ingredients of agricultural origin.

item.num:
b.
Amended by No I of the O of 2 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 738).
item.p: Additives, processing aids, flavouring substances and flavouring preparations, water, salt, preparations of microorganisms and enzymes, minerals (including trace elements), vitamins and amino acids, and other micronutrients in foodstuffs shall only be used if they have been authorised for use in organic production in accordance with Article 16k.

Only non-organically produced ingredients
Term in accordance with No I of the O of 31 Oct. 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 6353). which have been authorised according to Article 16k are used.
An organic ingredient may not be used together with the same non-organic ingredient or one produced during conversion.

item.num:
e.
Repealed by Annex No 1 of the O of 27 May 2020, with effect from 1 July 2020 (AS 2020 2229).

item.p: the product or its ingredients have not been treated with ionising radiation.

content.p: No substances may be used and no processes applied which restore properties lost in the processing and storage of organic foodstuffs or correct the result of negligent processing, or could otherwise be misleading with regard to the actual quality of these products.

The EAER may restrict or prohibit the use of certain processes and treatments.
Inserted by No I of the O of 2 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 738).

article.heading: Criteria for the authorisation of products and substances under Article 16j paragraph 2 letters b and c for processing

blockList.listIntroduction: In agreement with the Federal Department of Home Affairs (FDHA), the EAER shall lay down which products and substances under Article 16j paragraph 2 letters b and c are authorised for processing. Products and substances shall be authorised if the following conditions are met:

item.p: No permitted alternatives according to this ordinance are available.
Without these substances and ingredients, the foodstuff cannot be produced, or preserved, or specific nutritional requirements cannot be met.

content.p: Products and substances under Article 16j paragraph 2 letter b must occur in nature and have undergone only mechanical, physical, biological, enzyme or microbiological processes, unless the products and substances concerned are not available on the market in sufficient quantity or quality from such sources.

blockList.listIntroduction: In derogation from the principle laid down in Article 3 letter c, the EAER may authorise substances under Article 16j paragraph 2 letter b which have been produced using genetically modified organisms if:

item.p: they cannot be replaced by other substances; and

they are not available on the market manufactured in any other way.
Inserted by No I of the O of 31 Oct. 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 6353).

blockList.listIntroduction: Where an ingredient of agricultural origin has not been authorised by the EAER under Article 16j paragraph 2 letter c, FOAG may authorise its use in certain end products for a maximum period of six months on application if the provisions of the legislation on foodstuffs are complied with and there is a temporary shortage. The application must show:

item.p: that a shortage exists;
that the end product cannot be manufactured in any other way;
details of the probable duration of the shortage;

what measures are to be taken to remedy it.
Amended by No I of the O of 2 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 738).

content.p:
The authorisation under paragraph 3 may be renewed twice for a maximum of six months each time.
Inserted by No I of the O of 2 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 738).

The EAER may set out further criteria for authorisation or withdrawal of authorisation for products and substances under paragraph 3.
Inserted by No I of the O of 2 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 738).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 31 Oct. 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 6353).

article.heading: Specific principles for the production of processed organic animal feedingstuffs

blockList.listIntroduction: In addition to the general principles laid down in Article 3, the following principles apply to the production of processed organic animal feedingstuffs:

item.p: The use of feed additives and processing aids must be kept to the minimum and limited to cases where this is an essential technological or zootechnical imperative or serves particular nutritional purposes.
Substances and production methods which could be misleading with regard to the actual quality of the product are not permitted.
Animal feedingstuffs must be processed with care, if possible using organic, mechanical and physical methods

article.heading:
Provisions for the production of processed organic animal feedingstuffs
Amended by No I of the O of 31 Oct. 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 6353).

content.p: The production of processed organic animal feedingstuffs must be carried out separately in time or space from the production of non-organic feedingstuffs.
An organic animal feed material may not be used together with the same non-organically produced animal feed material.

Animal feed materials which are used or further processed in the production of organic animal feedingstuffs must not have been produced using chemically synthesised solvents.
Inserted by No I of the O of 31 Oct. 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 6353).

No substances may be used and no processes employed which restore properties lost in the processing and storage of organic feedingstuffs or correct the result of careless processing, or could otherwise be misleading with regard to the actual nature of these products.

article.heading: Provisions for the production of organic yeast

content.p: Only organically produced substrates may be used for the production of organic yeast. Other products and substances shall only be used if they are authorised under Article 16k for use in organic processing.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 31 Oct. 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 6353).

article.heading: Provisions for the production of organic wine

content.p: The EAER shall lay down which methods, practices and processes are authorised for the production of organic wine.

FOAG may lay down that the use of sulphur dioxide is permitted for certain geographical areas, up to the maximum values laid down in the legislation on foodstuffs, if abnormal weather conditions in a particular crop year affect the health of organic grapes in these areas due to serious bacterial or fungal infestation and if this means that more sulphur dioxide than in previous years has to be used in order to obtain a comparable end product.
Amended by No I of the O of 29 Oct. 2014, in force since 1 Jan. 2015 (AS 2014 3969).

Chapter 3

article.heading:
Products not intended for human consumption
Inserted by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009, in force since 1 Jan. 2010 (AS 2009 6317).

blockList.listIntroduction: Products which are not intended for human consumption may only be labelled as organic products if:

item.p: the labelling clearly refers to the agricultural production;
they were organically produced or prepared or imported in accordance with Article 22;

item.num:
c.
Amended by No I of the O of 10 Nov. 2004, in force since 1 Jan. 2005 (AS 2004 4891).
item.p: they were produced, prepared, imported, stored or marketed by an operator who is subject to an inspection system laid down in Chapter 5;

item.num:
d.
Repealed by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009, with effect from 1 Jan. 2010 (AS 2009 6317).

content.p:
The EAER may lay down additional rules for feedingstuffs, plant propagating material and seeds for cultivation.
Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2000 (AS 2000 2491). Amended by No I of the O of 12 Nov. 2008, in force since 1 Jan. 2009 (AS 2008 5823).

Inserted by No I of the O of 7 Nov. 2001 (AS 2001 3542). Repealed by No I of the O of 26 Nov. 2003, with effect from 1 Jan. 2004 (AS 2003 5347).

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009, in force since 1 Jan. 2010 (AS 2009 6317).

blockList.listIntroduction: The indications laid down in Article 2 paragraph 2 may be used in the product description for processed foodstuffs provided that:

item.p: the foodstuff meets the requirements laid down in Article 16j;
at least 95 per cent by weight of the ingredients of agricultural origin were organically produced;

content.p: The indications laid down in Article 2 paragraph 2 may be used in the list of ingredients, provided that the foodstuff meets the requirements laid down in Article 16j paragraph 1 and paragraph 2 letters a, b and d–f.

blockList.listIntroduction: The indications laid down in Article 2 paragraph 2 may be used in the list of ingredients and in the same field of vision as the product description provided that:

item.p: the main ingredient is a game or fishing product;
all other ingredients of agricultural origin are purely organic;
the foodstuff meets the requirements laid down in Article 16j paragraph 1 and paragraph 2 letters a, b and d–f.

content.p: An indication is given in the list of ingredients which ingredients are organically produced.

If an indication is used in accordance with paragraph 2 or 3, the reference to organic production may only be made in connection with the organic ingredients. The total percentage of organic ingredients in the ingredients of agricultural origin must be given in the list of ingredients.
The indications and percentage information laid down in paragraph 5 must appear in the same colour and in the same size and style of lettering as the other information in the list of ingredients.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 2 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 738).

content.p: For flavourings, the indications specified in Article 2 paragraph 2 may be used only if they are flavouring preparations or natural flavouring substances authorised for processing in accordance with Article 16k and their flavouring components and carriers are all organic.

authorialNote.p: Repealed by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009, with effect from 1 Jan. 2010 (AS 2009 6317).

article.heading:
Products from holdings under conversion
Inserted by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009, in force since 1 Jan. 2010 (AS 2009 6317).

content.p:
Products labelled in accordance with Articles 17 or 18 paragraph 1 which were produced in holdings under conversion must also be marked with the indication ‘produced during conversion to organic farming’.
Amended by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009, in force since 1 Jan. 2010 (AS 2009 6317).
Products from holdings under conversion may not be labelled as organic products until four months after the date of conversion.
Such products must not give the impression that they come from fully converted holdings.

The colour, size and style of lettering of the reference to conversion may not be more prominent than the product description. The words ‘organic farming’ may not stand out more than the words ‘produced during conversion to’; the colour, size and style of lettering of references to organic farming may not be more prominent than the reference to conversion.

Ingredients of agricultural origin produced in holdings under conversion may be indicated as such by reference to the conversion in the other indications laid down in Article 18 paragraphs 2 and 3. They may not be included in the total percentage of organic ingredients laid down in Article 18 paragraph 5.
Amended by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009, in force since 1 Jan. 2010 (AS 2009 6317).

A reference to organic farming shall only appear in the product description if the product contains no more than one ingredient of agricultural origin.
Amended by No I of the O of 7 Dec. 1998, in force since 1 Jan. 1999 (AS 1999 399).

Products from holdings undergoing conversion in stages may omit the reference to conversion in their labelling once the relevant parcels have been under conversion for two years, provided that all sectors of the holding are under conversion.

authorialNote.p: Repealed by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009, with effect from 1 Jan. 2010 (AS 2009 6317).
Inserted by No I of the O of 26 Nov. 2003 (AS 2003 5347). Amended by No I of the O of 31 Oct. 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 6353).

article.heading:
Labelling of feedingstuffs for production animals
Amended by No I of the O of 6 Nov. 2024, in force since 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 687).

blockList.listIntroduction: The indications laid down in Article 2 paragraph 2 may be used on processed animal feedingstuffs provided the following requirements are met:

item.p: The processed animal feedingstuff complies with the provisions of this Ordinance, in particular Articles 16a, 16kbis and 16l and their implementing provisions.
All ingredients of plant or animal origin contained in the processed animal feedingstuff consist of organic animal feed materials.
At least 95 per cent of the dry matter of the product consists of animal feed materials of organic origin.

content.p: In the case of processed animal feedingstuffs which do not comply with one of the requirements laid down in paragraph 1 letters b or c, only the indication ‘may be used in organic farming in accordance with the Organic Farming Ordinance’ may be used.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 26 Nov. 2003, in force since 1 July 2004 (AS 2003 5347).

article.heading:
Further labelling requirements of feedingstuffs for production animals
Amended by No I of the O of 6 Nov. 2024, in force since 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 687).

blockList.listIntroduction: The indications referred to in Article 21a must meet the following requirements:

item.p: they must not be more prominent than the description or name of the animal feedingstuff due to their colour, format or style of lettering;

with reference to the organic matter, they must indicate in the same field of vision the percentage of animal feedingstuffs which were produced on organic land and the percentage of animal feedingstuffs which were produced on land under conversion;

item.num:
c.
Repealed by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009, with effect from 1 Jan. 2010 (AS 2009 6317).

item.p: they must give a list of the names of the animal feed materials produced organically or under conversion to organic farming.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 6 Nov. 2024, in force since 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 687).

blockList.listIntroduction: The indications laid down in Article 2 paragraph 2 may be used in the product description and the details on the composition for processed feedingstuffs for pets provided that:

item.p: the feedingstuff meets the requirements laid down in Articles 16a paragraphs 2 and 7, 16kbis and 16l; and
at least 95 per cent by weight of the ingredients of agricultural origin were organically produced.

blockList.listIntroduction: The indications laid down in Article 2 paragraph 2 may be used only in the details on the composition for processed feedingstuffs for pets provided that:

item.p: less than 95 per cent by weight of the ingredients of agricultural origin were organically produced;
only feed additives and processing aids permitted under Article 16a are used in the processing of the feedingstuff; and
the feedingstuff meets the requirements laid down in Articles 16a paragraphs 2 and 7, 16kbis and 16l.

blockList.listIntroduction: The indications laid down in Article 2 paragraph 2 may be used in the details on the composition and in the same field of vision as the product description provided that:

item.p: the main ingredient is a game or fishing product;
all other ingredients of agricultural origin are purely organic; and
the feedingstuff meets the requirements laid down in Articles 16a paragraphs 2 and 7, 16kbis and 16l.

content.p: It must be stated in the details on the composition which animal feed materials are organically produced.

If an indication is used in accordance with paragraph 2 or 3, the reference to organic production may only be made in connection with the organic ingredients. The total percentage of organic ingredients in the ingredients of agricultural origin must be given in the details on the composition.

The indications and percentage information laid down in paragraph 5 must appear in the same colour and in the same size and style of lettering as the other information in the details on the composition.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009, in force since 1 Jan. 2010 (AS 2009 6317).

blockList.listIntroduction: The code number of the certification body responsible for the operator who carried out the most recent production or processing operation must be given. The code number must meet the following requirements:

item.p: It must begin with the abbreviation for the country laid down in the international standard for two-letter country codes ISO 3166.
It must contain an indication referring to organic production.
It must contain a reference number issued by the Swiss accreditation body or by the competent authority in the case of products certified by bodies abroad.

content.p:
FOAG may issue instructions regarding the format of code numbers.
Inserted by No I of the O of 27 Oct. 2010, in force since 1 Jan. 2011 (AS 2010 5859).

blockList.listIntroduction: Imported products may be labelled as organic products if:

item.num:
a.
Amended by No I of the O of 18 Nov. 2009, in force since 1 Jan. 2010 (AS 2009 6317).
item.p: they have been produced and prepared in accordance with rules which are equivalent to those laid down in Chapters 2, 2a and 3;

item.num:
b.
Amended by No I of the O of 2. Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 738).

content.p: FOAG may carry out random checks on the certification bodies and inspection authorities.

content.p: For meat production, all necessary inspections must be carried out at all stages of production, slaughter, cutting and any other preparation up to the sale to the consumer, to ensure that, as far as technically possible, the origin and position of the animal products in the production, processing and preparation chain can be certified from the unit of production of the livestock to the final packaging and/or labelling unit.

blockList.listIntroduction: Certification bodies must apply to be licensed by FOAG for their activities under this Ordinance. In order to be licensed, the certification bodies must:

item.p: have an established organisation and certification and inspection procedures (standard inspection programme) which, in particular, establish criteria that are binding on the operators subject to inspection, and a suitable programme of measures applicable if irregularities are noted;
have the expertise, equipment and infrastructure necessary to undertake the inspection and certification activities in accordance with this Ordinance;
have a sufficient number of employees who have sufficient expertise and knowledge of the elements affecting the organic status of products;
ensure that their employees have the necessary qualifications, education and experience in the area of organic production in general and of the provisions of this Ordinance in particular;
be independent and free of any conflict of interests with regard to the inspection and certification activities laid down in this Ordinance.

content.p: They must also carry out the tasks set out in Annex 1 and fulfil the obligations in Articles 30–30e.

The certification bodies must grant FOAG access to their premises and facilities and provide the information and support that FOAG deems necessary to carry out its duties. This includes cooperation with the inspection under the Swiss control system or with the peer review by foreign authorities.

FOAG may suspend or revoke the licence of a certification body if the certification body does not fulfil the requirements and conditions. FOAG shall notify the Swiss Accreditation Service (SAS) immediately of its decision.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 29 Oct. 2014, in force since 1 Jan. 2015 (AS 2014 3969).

content.p: The certification body shall carry out one inspection per operator at least once a year, or at least twice a year in the case of conversion in stages. It shall check to ensure that all operators subject to certification obligations fully comply with the provisions of this Ordinance.

In addition, the certification body shall carry out spot checks. The frequency of the spot checks depends on the risk assessment of the operators as laid down in Article 30abis; they must be carried out on at least 10 per cent of the operators subject to certification under paragraph 1.
At least 10 per cent of all inspection visits carried out under paragraphs 1 and 2 must be unannounced.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 27 Oct. 2010 (AS 2010 5859). Amended by No I of the O of 29 Oct. 2014, in force since 1 Jan. 2015 (AS 2014 3969).

content.p: The certification body must take samples and test them for production materials or production methods or traces thereof which are not permitted in organic production, if there is any suspicion that such production materials or methods are being used.
The certification body may also take and test samples in any other circumstances.

The number of samples which the certification body must take and test each year must amount to at least 5 per cent of the number of operators subject to its inspection. The selection of operators from whom samples are to be taken shall be in accordance with the general risk assessment for non-compliance with the provisions governing organic production. The general risk assessment shall include all stages of production, preparation and sale.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 29 Oct. 2014, in force since 1 Jan. 2015 (AS 2014 3969).

blockList.listIntroduction: The certification bodies shall submit to FOAG documentation concerning their risk assessment procedure for operators subject to their inspection. The risk assessment shall take account of the results of earlier inspections, the quantity of affected products and the risk of mixing organic with non-organic goods. The risk assessment shall be the basis for establishing:

item.p: the scope of the unannounced or announced annual inspections;
the contracted operators on whom additional spot checks are carried out under Article 30 paragraph 2;
the inspection visits carried out under Article 30 paragraph 3 which are unannounced;
the operators on whom unannounced inspections and visits are to be carried out.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 29 Oct. 2014 (AS 2014 3969). Amended by No I of the O of 2 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 738).

content.p: The certification body under Articles 23a, 28 or 29 or, if appropriate, the inspection authority under Article 23a shall issue a relevant certificate to each operator subject to its inspections which meets the requirements of this Ordinance in its area of operations. The certificate must indicate, as a minimum, the identity of the operator, the category of products to which the certificate applies and the expiry date of the certificate.

animals and unprocessed animal products;
algae and unprocessed aquaculture products;
processed agricultural products and processed aquaculture products intended for use as food;
feedingstuffs;
wine;

other products.
Amended by No I of the O of 6 Nov. 2024, in force since 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 687).

content.p: The certificate may also be issued in electronic form provided that its authenticity is guaranteed by a recognised electronic method which is proof against forgery.

article.heading: Obligation to notify and exchange of information

content.p: If the operator or his contractors are inspected by different certification bodies, or by a third party commissioned by them, then the participating certification bodies shall exchange the relevant information concerning the operations which they have inspected among themselves or with the third parties commissioned by them.

The certification body shall notify FOAG and the competent cantonal food inspection agencies immediately if an operator or his contractor subject to its inspections changes to another certification body.
The previous certification body shall hand over to the new certification body the relevant parts of the inspection dossier of the operator in question and the reports laid down in 1.1.4 of Annex 1.
The new certification body shall ensure that the operator has rectified any non-conformities noted in the report of the previous certification body or is in the process of doing so.
